direct_cause.statement: The manuscript defines delta_AB as an onsite-energy difference but inserts the same symbol as the sigma_z coefficient, producing a factor-two conflict.

root_cause.statement: The paper simultaneously defines delta_AB as epsilon_A-epsilon_B and multiplies sigma_z by delta_AB, which mathematically produces the difference 2 delta_AB. Both executable convention branches preserve the phase order but cannot make those two printed statements equivalent.

code_fault_assessment.statement: Both convention branches use the same tested evolution code; exact Pauli eigenvalue algebra, converged gap scans and independent winding/Chern methods exclude a numerical factor-two artifact.

checks.statement: Both coefficient readings are explicit in the frozen config and output, with no hidden parameter fit.
Both transition sequences are stable on the paper-scale momentum grid.
diag(delta,-delta) has onsite-energy difference 2 delta, whereas diag(delta/2,-delta/2) realizes the printed epsilon_A-epsilon_B definition.
Full-evolution winding and gauge-aware Fukui Chern calculations independently preserve the same phase ordering.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A shared strip-gauge or phase-boundary implementation error cannot change the exact two-level identity between a sigma_z coefficient and its onsite-energy difference.

next_discriminating_test.expected_resolution: The review will decide whether the stable source discrepancy qualifies as a paper error or remains a notation-level ambiguity.
